---
rg: 2
id: kassabov-subspace-angle-criterion
kind: claim
title: A group generated by finite subgroups has property (T) when the pairwise fixed-space angle cosines give a positive definite matrix
---

**Statement.** Let `G` be a group generated by finite subgroups `G_1, …, G_n`. Suppose there are
numbers `ε_ij` such that, for every unitary representation `H` of `G` and all `i ≠ j`,

```text
cos ∢(H^{G_i}, H^{G_j}) <= ε_ij ,
```

where `∢` is the Friedrichs angle: `cos ∢(V_1, V_2)` is the supremum of `|<v_1, v_2>|` over unit
vectors `v_i ∈ V_i` orthogonal to `V_1 ∩ V_2`. If one subspace contains the other, there is no such
vector, the supremum over the empty set is `0`, and the angle is `π/2` (Kassabov, Remark 3.4). If the
symmetric `n × n` matrix with `1` on the diagonal and `-ε_ij` off the diagonal is positive definite,
then `G` has Kazhdan's property (T).

**ESTABLISHED (literature import).** Kassabov's Theorem 1.2 gives a lower bound
`∢(V_1, …, V_n) >= φ > 0` for every configuration of closed subspaces with these pairwise bounds, and
`φ` depends only on the matrix. His Observation 2.1 turns a lower bound on
`∢(H^{G_1}, …, H^{G_n})` that holds in every unitary representation into property (T) when the `G_i`
are finite. See `kassabov-subspace-angle-criterion-citation`.

**Calibration.**
- *Uniform case.* With every `ε_ij = ε` and `n = 3`, the matrix is positive definite iff `ε < 1/2`.
  This is the Ershov–Jaikin-Zapirain bound `ε < 1/(n-1)`, and it contains Żuk's criterion (link spectral
  gap `λ_1 > 1/2`) for triangles of groups.
- *Coxeter check (a trivial model must fail).* For a Coxeter triangle group with generators `s_i` and
  `m_ij = ord(s_i s_j)`, one has `ε_ij = cos(π/m_ij)`, and the matrix is the Tits Gram matrix. It is positive
  definite exactly for the finite Coxeter groups, which have (T). The affine triangle groups have
  determinant zero, and the hyperbolic ones have indefinite matrices; neither has (T). So the criterion
  is sharp on the model where it must fail.

Used by `kazhdan-hyperbolic-sl2-root-triangles`.
